name: Deadline
label: Dischord
lede: A fifteen-year-old drummer's first band, three songs on Flex Your Head, a night opening for Flipper, and a final session that waited five years for a record.

eras.title: Fifteen and behind the kit
eras.text: Summer 1981 was D.C. hardcore's first big churn: bands dying, new ones forming out of the pieces. Deadline were four kids starting from scratch, including Brendan Canty, a drummer who'd just picked up sticks.

years.h: Deadline forms: Hare, Caron, Scanlon and Canty
years.p: Ray Hare sings, Christian Caron plays guitar, Terry Scanlon bass, and [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] drums. Canty, born in 1966, started drumming at fifteen; Deadline is his first band.

eras.title: A year of shows and one last tape
eras.text: 1982 was Deadline's whole public life. They were on Flex Your Head, the Dischord sampler everyone in D.C. owned, played rooms like the 9:30 club, and went into Inner Ear one more time before calling it.

years.h: Deadline's first demo closes out Flex Your Head
years.p: Three songs from Deadline's September 1981 demo with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] at Inner Ear, Stolen Youth, Hear the Cry and Aftermath, are the last three tracks on Dischord's sampler. Deadline get the final word.

years.h: Deadline opens for [[Flipper|4e99b3a5-654b-43ee-a9bf-c55c155c0495]] at the 9:30 club
years.p: Dischord lists opening for San Francisco's Flipper at the 9:30 club among Deadline's memorable 1982 shows.
A month after their August 2 session at Inner Ear, Deadline is done. Dischord dates the run from summer 1981 to September 1982.

years.h: Live at the Wilson Center, June 25, 1982
yt: Live at the Wilson Center, June 25, 1982

eras.title: The drummer goes on, the tape comes out
eras.text: Deadline drummer Brendan Canty went on to play in Rites of Spring and Fugazi. Five years after Deadline's final session, the tape finally became a record, 8/2/82.

years.p: Brendan Canty helps start Rites of Spring with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] and [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]], the band at the center of Revolution Summer.
Brendan Canty replaces Colin Sears behind the kit in Fugazi, where he'll stay until the 2003 hiatus.

years.h: Deadline's last session comes out as 8/2/82
years.p: Deadline recorded eleven songs at Inner Ear on August 2, 1982, their final session. Five years later Peterbilt put them out as a one-sided 12-inch named for the date, since out of print.
years.xp:
The tape went unreleased and became, in Dischord's words, one of the great lost gems of D.C. punk. The date, 8/2/82, became the title.

The songs include Nothing for Me, Apathy, Outside the Law, Deep Sixed and Authority Figures.

eras.title: Found again
eras.text: Dischord folded Deadline into the label's own history and brought the lost session back.

years.p: Deadline appear on Dischord's anniversary box set, 20 Years of Dischord, and its companion collection of rare and unreleased tracks.
Deadline's 8/2/82, first issued by Peterbilt, gets a CD reissue as Dischord 161.5. Today Dischord offers it only as a digital download, and the comments under it are mostly people asking for vinyl.
